vedanga: One of the six limbs that support the Vedas: shiksha (sound), kalpa (ritual), vyakarana (grammar), nirukta (word origins), chandas (metre) and jyotisha (time and the heavens). Jyotisha is called the eye of the Veda.
siddhanta: The astronomy and calculation branch of Jyotish: planetary positions, eclipses, the calendar. It is the exact, checkable part.
hora: The branch that reads the individual birth chart and its timing. Also called Jataka. The word hora also names a planetary hour in muhurta.
samhita: The branch that covers the wider world: omens, weather, nations, buildings and auspicious times.
convention: The set of calculation choices behind a chart: ayanamsa, node type, house system, dasha year length, karaka scheme and matching tables. Two charts for the same birth can differ if the profile differs, so every chart and prediction should name its profile.
kp: Krishnamurti Paddhati. A system that uses Placidus houses, its own ayanamsa and a table of 249 star-and-sub divisions, and judges events by the sub-lord of house cusps.
meannode: Rahu and Ketu can be placed at the mean lunar node (a smooth average) or the true node (the actual momentary crossing of the Moon's orbit). The two can differ by more than a degree.
karakascheme: The Jaimini method that ranks planets by degree within their sign. The highest degree is the Atmakaraka. Texts allow seven planets or eight (adding Rahu), so the ranking can change.
ashtakoota: The eight-part, 36-point method of matching two charts by Moon nakshatra. Point tables differ slightly between almanacs.
savana: A year of exactly 360 days. Some dasha systems use it. A Vimshottari dasha counted in savana years runs about 100 days shorter per Saturn period than one counted in 365.25-day years.
ledger: A written log of predictions made before the outcome is known: window, area of life, a testable statement, convention profile, base rate and confidence. It is locked when written and scored later by the criteria written at the time.
boundary: A flag on any point (planet, lagna) lying within about 2° of a sign or nakshatra edge, because a small change in ayanamsa or birth time can move it across the edge.
retrieval: Studying by pulling an answer from memory, such as a quiz or a recall question, instead of rereading the material.
mastery: In this course, a score of 70% or more on a stage test, which unlocks the next stage.
graha: “That which seizes.” The nine moving influences: Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu. They are the actors of the chart.
rashi: A sign: one of 12 equal 30° slices of the sidereal zodiac. A planet in a sign takes on that sign’s style.
bhava: A house: an area of life. In whole-sign houses the lagna sign is house 1, the next sign house 2, and so on.
nakshatra: A lunar mansion: one of 27 slices of 13°20′. The Moon spends about a day in each. Your Moon’s nakshatra starts your dasha clock.
pada: A quarter of a nakshatra, 3°20′ wide. 108 padas in all; each pada equals one navamsa (D9) sign.
lagna: The ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth. It changes about every 2 hours, which is why the exact birth time matters.
ayanamsa: The gap between the tropical and sidereal zodiacs, about 24° today and growing by about 50″ a year. Lahiri (Chitrapaksha) is the Indian government standard.
sidereal: A zodiac fixed to the stars. Jyotish uses it. It sits about 24° behind the tropical zodiac.
tropical: A zodiac fixed to the seasons (0° Aries = the March equinox). Western astrology uses it.
kendra: Angular houses 1, 4, 7, 10: the pillars of the chart. Planets here act strongly and visibly.
trikona: Trine houses 1, 5, 9: houses of merit and fortune. Their lords are counted auspicious, though a second lordship (for example of a dusthana) can mix the result.
dusthana: Difficult houses 6, 8, 12: disease and debt, sudden change, loss. Their lords placed in each other can give Viparita Raja Yoga, success through adversity.
upachaya: Growing houses 3, 6, 10, 11: results improve with time and effort. Malefics do well here.
karaka: Significator. A planet that naturally stands for something, whatever the chart: Sun = father, Moon = mother, Venus = wife, Jupiter = children and husband.
dasha: A planetary period. In the Vimshottari system a 120-year cycle is shared by the nine planets; the running dasha lord decides which promises open now.
gochar: Transit: where the planets are moving now, read against the birth chart.
dignity: How comfortable a planet is in a sign: exalted (best), moolatrikona, own sign, friend’s, neutral, enemy’s, debilitated (weakest).
vargottama: A planet in the same sign in D1 and D9. Treated as strong and reliable. Your Mercury is vargottama in Gemini.
retrograde: A planet that appears to move backward from Earth. Classically it gains strength but delivers in an unusual or delayed way.
combust: A planet too close to the Sun, its light swallowed. It loses some independence. Your Mars is about 11° from the Sun, inside the 17° orb given for Mars in the Surya Siddhanta and BPHS tables. Some teachers use smaller orbs or ignore combustion across a sign edge (your Mars is in Taurus, the Sun in Gemini).
neechabhanga: Cancellation of debilitation. Rule sets differ by text: Phaladeepika and BPHS-style rules look at the lord of the debilitation or exaltation sign in a kendra from the lagna or Moon; another rule uses the planet that exalts in the debilitation sign; a later rule uses the debilitated planet itself in a kendra from the Moon. Your Saturn (debilitated in Aries) is a cancellation candidate under two of the later rules: the Sun, exalted in Aries, is in your 10th, and Saturn is in a kendra (10th) from your Moon. The lords of Aries and Libra (Mars, Venus) are not in a kendra, so the first rule set does not apply. A later stage tests each rule set.
ida: The lunar channel, felt as breath flowing through the left nostril. Cooling, receptive, steady.
pingala: The solar channel, felt as breath flowing through the right nostril. Heating, active, forceful.
sushumna: The central channel, when both nostrils flow equally. Classically unsuited for worldly action, suited for meditation.
tattva: The five elements in Swara Shastra: earth, water, fire, air, ether. Each is said to predominate in turn within each nostril’s flow of about an hour.
swara: In Swara Shastra, the breath and which nostril it flows through at a given moment.
precession: The slow wobble of Earth's axis, about 50.3″ a year, which moves the equinox point backwards through the stars. It is the reason the tropical and sidereal zodiacs drift apart.
ut: The time at the Greenwich meridian. Every planetary position is computed for a moment in UT. Clock time becomes UT by subtracting the time-zone offset in force at that place and date.
ist: Indian Standard Time · भारतीय मानक समय
UT plus 5 hours 30 minutes, based on the 82.5° E meridian, in force from 1 January 1906. It was advanced by one hour during the Second World War.
lmt: Time set by the longitude of a place alone: 4 minutes for each degree east of Greenwich. Satna (80.83° E) is 5 h 23 m 19 s ahead of UT.
siderealtime: Time measured by the stars rather than the Sun. Local sidereal time is the right ascension of the point crossing the meridian, which fixes which part of the zodiac is rising.
ramc: Right ascension of the mid-heaven: local sidereal time expressed in degrees (hours × 15). It is the input from which the ascendant is calculated.
wholesign: Each house is one complete sign. The lagna sign is house 1, the next sign is house 2, and so on. It is the default in most Parashari teaching, and the sign-based techniques of Jaimini assume it.
bhavachalit: A house system in which the middle of each house (bhava madhya) is found by dividing the arc from lagna to the 10th cusp, and house boundaries (sandhi) fall midway between neighbouring middles. Planets near sign edges can move to a neighbouring house.
placidus: A time-based system that divides the arcs the ecliptic travels above and below the horizon into three equal times. Houses are unequal. KP uses it.
panchang: The five-limbed almanac: tithi, vara, nakshatra, yoga and karana. It is the calendar part of Jyotish and is pure astronomy.
tithi: A lunar day: each 12° of increase in the Moon's lead over the Sun. There are 30 in a lunar month, 15 in each paksha.
vara: The weekday, from sunrise to the next sunrise, ruled by the planet that gives it its name.
pyoga: One of 27 divisions made from the sum of the Sun's and the Moon's sidereal longitudes, each 13°20′ wide. Not the same thing as a planetary yoga (combination) in a chart.
karana: Half a tithi (6° of the Moon's lead over the Sun). There are 60 karana slots in a month using 11 names: 7 movable that repeat and 4 fixed.
gana: The temperament class of a nakshatra: Deva (gentle, god-like), Manushya (human, mixed), Rakshasa (forceful, strongly driven). Rakshasa does not mean evil. Used in matching and in character reading.
yoni: The “animal” assigned to each nakshatra, 14 animals in male and female pairs. It stands for instinct and physical temperament and is used in matching (4 points).
nadi: A three-way classification of the 27 nakshatras: Adi, Madhya, Antya, linked to the humours Vata, Pitta, Kapha. In matching it carries the most points (8).
shakti: The specific power or function given to a nakshatra in the tradition that follows the Taittiriya Brahmana, for example “power to burn” for Krittika.
purushartha: The four aims of life: dharma (duty), artha (wealth and means), kama (desire) and moksha (liberation). Modern tables assign one aim to each nakshatra as its underlying motivation.
muhurta: Choosing a favourable time for an action. Nakshatra class, tara bala and chandra bala are three of its basic filters.
navamsa: The ninth division (D9) of a sign: nine slices of 3°20′ each. Every pada of a nakshatra falls in exactly one navamsa. The D9 chart is read for strength and for marriage.
abhijit: A short 28th nakshatra between Uttara Ashadha and Shravana, used in some muhurta traditions. The Vimshottari dasha and this course use 27 equal nakshatras.
gandanta: “Knot at the end.” The junction where a water sign ends and a fire sign begins, the last part of Ashlesha, Jyeshtha and Revati and the first part of Magha, Mula and Ashwini. Traditionally a sensitive zone for the Moon at birth.
tarabala: A daily check. Count from your birth nakshatra to the day’s Moon nakshatra, divide by 9 and read the remainder as one of nine taras, some good and some bad.
chandrabala: A daily check. The Moon’s transit sign counted from your natal Moon sign: houses 1, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11 are favourable, 4, 8, 12 unfavourable.
chandrashtama: The Moon transiting the 8th sign from your natal Moon sign, about two and a quarter days each month. The classic day to avoid new starts.
vimshottari: The 120-year dasha system. Nine planets share 120 years in a fixed order; the starting point comes from the Moon’s nakshatra at birth.
mahadasha: The major period of one planet in the Vimshottari system, from 6 to 20 years.
antardasha: A sub-period inside a mahadasha. Each mahadasha splits among all nine planets in proportion to their years.
bhogya: The part of the first mahadasha that remains at birth. It equals the lord’s years multiplied by the fraction of the Moon’s nakshatra still to be crossed.
starlord: The lord of the nakshatra a planet occupies. Many teachers say a planet delivers its results through its star lord as well as its sign lord.
exaltation: The sign where a planet is strongest. BPHS gives the deepest point inside it: Sun 10° Aries, Moon 3° Taurus, Mars 28° Capricorn, Mercury 15° Virgo, Jupiter 5° Cancer, Venus 27° Pisces, Saturn 20° Libra.
debilitation: The sign opposite a planet’s exaltation, where it is weakest. The deepest fall point is the same degree as the deepest exaltation point, in the opposite sign.
moolatrikona: A stretch of one sign where a planet is treated as a little stronger than in the rest of its own sign. For the Sun it is Leo 0°–20°.
swakshetra: A sign ruled by the planet. The Sun and Moon own one sign each; the other five planets own two.
ucchabala: Exaltation strength: the planet’s angular distance from its deepest fall point, divided by 3, giving 0 to 60 virupas. It is the first part of Sthana bala in Shadbala (BPHS ch. 27).
maitri: The relationship between two planets: friend, neutral or enemy. It decides how comfortable a planet is in the other’s sign.
tatkalika: Temporary friendship, read from one chart: planets in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 10th, 11th or 12th from each other are friends; in the 1st, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th or 9th they are enemies.
panchadha: The five-fold relationship: natural and temporary friendship combined into great friend, friend, neutral, enemy or great enemy.
grahayuddha: Two of Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn within 1° of longitude. One planet is judged the winner and the other the loser; the loser is said to lose strength.
cheshta: Motional strength in Shadbala. A retrograde (vakra) planet gets the maximum, 60 virupas, in the BPHS scheme.
functional: A planet’s nature for one particular lagna, decided by the houses it rules, not by its natural nature. Jupiter is a natural benefic but can be a functional malefic.
yogakaraka: A planet that rules both a kendra and a trikona for a given lagna (for example Saturn for Libra lagna). The Parashari texts treat it as the most helpful planet for that lagna.
maraka: A planet tied to the 2nd and 7th houses, the houses that stand twelfth from the longevity houses 3 and 8. In practice it signals strain on vitality in its periods; it is not a death sentence.
kendradhipati: The blemish a natural benefic is said to take when it rules a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th). The lagna lord is excused.
drishti: Planetary aspect, the Parashari kind: every planet sees the 7th house; Mars also sees the 4th and 8th, Jupiter the 5th and 9th, Saturn the 3rd and 10th.
rashidrishti: Sign aspect, the Jaimini kind: movable signs see the fixed signs except the adjacent one, fixed signs see the movable signs except the adjacent one, dual signs see the other dual signs.
bhavesha: The planet that rules the sign on a house. Its own sign, house, dignity and company decide how that house delivers.
viparita: Success through reversal: the lord of the 6th, 8th or 12th sits in another of those three houses. Your Saturn, 6th lord in the 8th, forms the Harsha variety.
asta: Combustion. See also the Stage 1 term “combust”. The Sun’s closeness weakens a planet; the orb differs by planet.
pratyantar: A sub-sub-period inside an antardasha, a few weeks to a few months long.
dasasandhi: The junction between two periods. Many astrologers treat the months around a mahadasha change as a transition zone. The idea is widely used; no classical source for it is cited in this course.
vedha: In gochar, a planet in a normally good house from the Moon gives less if another planet stands in its paired obstruction house.
sadesati: The roughly seven-and-a-half years when Saturn passes through the 12th, 1st and 2nd signs from the natal Moon sign. It is a popular tradition and is not found as such in BPHS.
dhaiya: Saturn in the 4th or 8th sign from the natal Moon sign, about two and a half years each. Popular tradition, not found in BPHS.
dwigochar: Jupiter and Saturn both influencing the same house or sign by occupation or aspect at the same time. A timing filter, not an event by itself.
ashtakavarga: A scoring system in which each planet (and the lagna) gives marks to the 12 signs. BPHS uses it for transit judgement; modern software counts benefic marks, called bindus.
bindu: In modern usage, a benefic point in Ashtakavarga. BPHS (Santhanam’s translation) calls the benefic mark a rekha (line) and the malefic mark a bindu (dot), the reverse of modern use.
grahan: A solar or lunar eclipse. Traditions look at which natal points the eclipse degree touches and over what orb, and many ignore penumbral lunar eclipses.
yoga: A named combination of planets, signs and houses that a text links to a result. A yoga is a promise with conditions: it needs to be formed, strong, uncancelled and activated by a dasha before it shows in life.
mahapurusha: Five “great person” yogas made when Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn sits in a kendra in its own or exaltation sign: Ruchaka, Bhadra, Hamsa, Malavya, Shasha.
rajayoga: A “royal” yoga: a link between the lord of a kendra and the lord of a trikona, usually by conjunction, mutual aspect or exchange. It signals status, authority and visible achievement in the planets’ periods.
dhanayoga: A wealth combination: a link between the lords of the money houses (2, 5, 9, 11, with the lagna lord) by conjunction, aspect, exchange or placement in each other’s houses.
chandrayoga: Yogas counted from the Moon: Sunapha (planet in 2nd from Moon), Anapha (12th), Durudhara (both), Kemadruma (neither), Gajakesari (Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon; BPHS also allows the lagna and adds conditions), Adhi (benefics in 6th, 7th, 8th from the Moon). The Sun and the nodes are usually not counted.
suryayoga: Yogas counted from the Sun: Vesi (planet in 2nd from Sun), Vosi (12th), Ubhayachari (both). The Moon and the nodes are not counted. Budh-Aditya, Sun with Mercury, is the best-known solar yoga.
parivartana: Exchange of signs: two planets each sit in the sign the other rules. Both gain strength. Maha (between lords of good houses), Khala (involving the 3rd lord) and Dainya (involving a 6th, 8th or 12th lord) describe its quality.
nabhasa: Pattern yogas based on the shape of the whole chart: the type of signs planets occupy (Ashraya), kendra placement (Dala), geometric shapes (Akriti) and the number of signs occupied (Sankhya). Broad in meaning, low in specific weight.
arishta: A classical term for an indication of danger or hardship, especially in infancy (balarishta), together with the conditions that cancel it (arishta bhanga). Not a modern prediction tool for death or disaster.
kalasarpa: A modern, debated pattern where all planets lie on one side of the Rahu-Ketu axis. Definitions, names and results vary widely between authors, and a classical source is not clear.
mangaldosha: Also Kuja dosha: Mars in certain houses (commonly 1, 4, 7, 8, 12, and 2 for some) counted from the lagna, Moon or Venus. Used mainly in marriage matching. Many exceptions and cancellations exist.
avastha: A state of a planet. Baladi avastha divides each sign into five 6° parts (infant, youth-boy, young, old, dead) and reads the planet’s results as stronger or weaker by that part.
varga: A divisional chart. A varga divides each 30° sign into equal or unequal parts and assigns each part to a sign. D9 means a division by nine, D10 by ten. The result is a second chart that zooms in on one area of life.
shodashavarga: The sixteen divisional charts of the Parashari system: D1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 9, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 27, 30, 40, 45, 60.
dashamsa: The D10 chart: each sign split into ten parts of 3°. Read for career, work and public action.
pushkara: Certain navamsa (and degree) segments said to “nourish” a planet placed in them. Tables of these segments differ between sources.
vimshopaka: A score out of twenty for a planet’s overall dignity across a chosen set of divisional charts (six, seven, ten or sixteen of them), with each chart weighted. Described in the Parashari texts; the engine does not compute it yet.
karakamsa: In Jaimini astrology, the navamsa sign of the Atmakaraka (the planet with the highest degree), read as a lagna for the soul’s purpose and vocation.
upapada: In Jaimini astrology, the arudha (image-house) of the 12th house. It is read for marriage and the partner’s role. The engine places it in Aries for your chart.
rectification: Adjusting an uncertain birth time until the chart’s timing methods match known life events. It needs reliable event dates and is itself a debated skill.
shadbala: “Six strengths”: the classical method for measuring a planet’s power with six components: positional, directional, temporal, motional, natural and aspectual strength. The result is stated in rupas.
rupa: The units of Shadbala. One rupa equals 60 virupas. Each planet has a required minimum in rupas (for example 6.5 for the Sun).
sthanabala: Positional strength: how well the planet is placed in its sign, in the divisional charts, in odd or even signs, in kendras and in its decanate.
digbala: Directional strength: each planet is strongest in one particular house (Jupiter and Mercury in the 1st, Sun and Mars in the 10th, Saturn in the 7th, Moon and Venus in the 4th) and weakest in the opposite house.
kalabala: Temporal strength: strength from the time of birth, such as day or night, bright or dark half of the month, the weekday, the hour and the planet’s declination.
cheshtabala: Motional strength: strength from the planet’s motion, mainly its speed and retrogression. The Sun and Moon use different measures in place of it.
naisargika: Natural strength: a fixed ranking, the same for everyone. The Sun is naturally strongest, then Moon, Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, Mars and Saturn.
drikbala: Aspectual strength: strength added or subtracted by the aspects of benefic and malefic planets.
bhavabala: The strength of a house, built from its lord’s strength, the house’s own directional strength, and the aspects falling on it.
bav: The individual chart of one planet: its bindus in each of the twelve signs. There are seven (Sun to Saturn); their totals are 48, 49, 39, 54, 56, 52 and 39.
sav: The combined chart: the sum of the seven BAVs in each sign. It totals 337 points over the twelve signs, an average of about 28 per sign.
kakshya: A subdivision of a sign into eight parts of 3°45′. Each is ruled by one of Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Lagna, in that order, and used to refine transit timing with Ashtakavarga.
shodhana: Reduction: classical arithmetic that “purifies” the Ashtakavarga totals (trikona shodhana, then ekadhipatya shodhana) before computing further figures. Described here only in outline.
chara_karaka: A movable significator. Jaimini ranks the planets by degree within their sign and gives each rank a life role (soul, minister, sibling, and so on). The roles change from chart to chart.
atmakaraka: The planet with the highest degree within its sign. Jaimini and BPHS call it the soul significator and the most important of the chara karakas.
rashi_drishti: Sign aspect, Jaimini’s system. Signs aspect signs, and every planet in an aspecting sign aspects every planet in the aspected sign. It does not use planet-specific aspects.
argala: “Bolt” or intervention. Planets in the 2nd, 4th and 11th from a house or planet (and secondarily the 5th) press on it and shape its results.
virodhargala: Obstruction of an argala. Planets in the 12th, 10th and 3rd (and 9th for the 5th) from the reference point can block the argala from the 2nd, 4th and 11th (5th).
arudha: The projected image of a house: how that house appears to the world, which can differ from what it really is. Each of the 12 houses has one.
chara_dasha: A Jaimini sign-based period system. Each sign rules a period whose length comes from counting to its lord’s sign.
narayana_dasha: A sign-based dasha taught in Sanjay Rath’s tradition. It begins from the stronger of the lagna and 7th house signs. Rules differ from Chara dasha.
prashna: “Question.” Horary astrology: a chart is cast for the moment a sincere question is asked, and read for that one question.
tara_bala: The strength of the day’s Moon nakshatra, counted from your birth nakshatra in nine groups (taras). Five groups are good (Sampat, Kshema, Sadhana, Mitra, Param Mitra), three are bad (Vipat, Pratyak, Naidhana) and one, Janma, is mixed.
chandra_bala: The strength of the day’s Moon sign, counted from your natal Moon sign. The 4th, 8th and 12th are avoided; the 8th (Chandrashtama) is the most avoided.
rahu_kaal: A daily period of about 90 minutes (one eighth of daylight) that tradition avoids for new starts. Its position depends on the weekday and on sunrise and sunset.
vishti: Also called Bhadra. The 7th movable karana, a half-tithi that occurs eight times a month. Traditionally avoided for auspicious beginnings.
lagna_shuddhi: Checking the rising sign at the chosen moment: the 8th house should be empty, the lagna lord strong, benefics in kendras and trikonas, malefics in the 3rd, 6th and 11th.
porutham: The ten matching checks of the southern (Tamil, Kerala) tradition. Rajju is treated as the most important.
mangal_dosha: Mars placed in certain houses (from lagna, and in some lists from the Moon or Venus). Said to strain marriage. Lists of houses and cancellations differ by region.
kalapurusha: The zodiac as a body: Aries is the head, Taurus the face and neck, and so on down to Pisces, the feet.
ingress: The moment a planet enters a sign. A mundane chart is cast for the Sun’s entry into Aries (Mesha Sankranti) to read the year for a country.
sub_lord: In KP, each nakshatra is divided into nine unequal parts in Vimshottari proportion. The planet ruling the part a point falls in is its sub lord, the decider of the result.
csl: The sub lord of a house cusp. In KP it decides whether the house’s matter will happen, through the houses it signifies.
significator: In KP, a planet “signifies” a house through four levels: planets in the star of an occupant, the occupants, planets in the star of the owner, and the owner.
varshaphala: The annual chart of the Tajika system, cast for the moment the Sun returns to its natal longitude. It reads one year at a time.
muntha: A point that starts at the natal lagna sign and moves one sign per year. Its house in the annual chart colours the year.
varshesha: The year lord: the strongest of five office-holders in the annual chart. It sets the tone of the year.
saham: An Arabic-derived sensitive point of the Tajika system, computed as lagna plus one planet minus another. Each stands for a theme (fortune, marriage, career).
ithasala: A Tajika yoga: a faster planet behind a slower one, within orb, in aspect. It shows a matter coming to completion. Its opposite, ishrafa, shows separation.
mudda_dasha: The Vimshottari sequence compressed into one year (about 3 days per Vimshottari year) for use inside a Tajika annual chart.
yogini_dasha: A 36-year cycle of eight periods named for eight yoginis, each tied to a planet. It is found from the Moon’s nakshatra number.
kalachakra: A sign-period system worked from the Moon’s nakshatra pada, using two zodiac wheels (savya and apasavya) and a “body” and “life” sign for each pada.
convention_profile: The full list of settings that produced a chart: ayanamsa, node type, house system, dasha year length, karaka scheme and matching table set. Every result should be quoted with its profile.
double_transit: A timing filter: a house is activated in a year when both Jupiter and Saturn, by occupation or aspect, reach it by transit. Attribution varies by source; the rule is a teaching framework, not a verified law.
brier: The average of (confidence minus outcome) squared, where the outcome is 1 if the event happened and 0 if not. Lower is better. Always saying 50% scores 0.25.
base_rate: How often an event happens anyway, for anyone of that age in a window of that length. A prediction is only informative if it beats this.
hindsight: After an outcome is known, people remember having expected it. Locked, timestamped entries are the remedy.
sensitivity: Repeating a reading under a second ayanamsa, the other node type, another dasha year length and a birth time a few minutes either side, then reporting whether the answer holds.
